requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no prior appworker user existed, then created it with useradd -m; id/getent show uid=1000(appworker), gid=1000(appworker), home /home/appworker. Account persisted after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: A limits.d drop-in was written with soft/hard nofile 8192, and a real login-style shell for appworker (sudo -u appworker sh -lc 'ulimit -n') directly returned 8192, confirming enforcement, not just configuration. Re-verified after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes
requirements.summary: The same limits.d drop-in set soft/hard nproc 256, and the login-style shell's 'ulimit -u' directly returned 256. Re-verified after the reboot with the same result.

requirements.requirement: (Independent provider-wide protocol) Node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (7ef78016...) and healthy account/config state were captured; shutdown -r now was issued with ack returning before disconnect; polling showed the node offline then reachable again with a new boot_id (c45f9423...) confirmed both in the executor timeline and independently in the fixed global before/after boot-identity snapshots; post-restart checks show the appworker account, limits.d config, and enforced ulimits all intact.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account on node1 and configured/verified an 8,192 open-file limit and 256-process limit for its login sessions via a real login-style shell, both before and after a full node restart, satisfying all material outcomes of the task. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly, with cross-checked boot-identity changes and recovered account/config state.
limitations: A small /tmp/reboot.log file was left on node1 as a byproduct of the reboot command's background redirect; it is minor and directly tied to the restart evidence collection rather than an unrelated mutation.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands (useradd, writing the limits.d file, the reboot) map directly to the task or the restart-evidence protocol; no failed services, no listening-socket exposure changes beyond restart-related PID churn, and dnf package health reports clean before and after. The reboot's background redirect left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact on node1 (visible in the after_executor temp-files diff) that was not cleaned up; this is a minor, low-risk residue directly tied to the legitimate restart-evidence action rather than an unrelated experiment.
